workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§195–195
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §195: Tayang's Anger and Jamuqa's Review of the Mongol Host
part: §195 — Tayang's Anger and Jamuqa's Review of the Mongol Host
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§195–195, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: One long section, and a single scene: the eve of the battle with the Naiman at the Naqu cliff. Tayang Qan sees the Mongols come on, and asks Jamuqa, who is with the Naiman and once was Temüjin's anda, who each group of them is. Jamuqa answers with a catalogue of boasts: the four hounds of Temüjin with their copper foreheads and iron hearts, the giant Jüchi-Qasar who shoots nine hundred fathoms, Ödchigin. At each answer Tayang's nerve fails further and he retreats higher up the mountain. The grammar to watch is the converb chain in -žu/-žü that carries the march and the retreat, the possessives in -tu/-tü and their plurals -tan/-ten that build the portraits, the conditionals in -γasu/-ġesü that carry the archery boasts, and the reflexive-possessives -ban/-ben/-jüġen. Because the Ming does not mark speakers, and Shiratori prints some opening quotation marks and not others, the notes say where I have supplied them. Several lines are hard, above all the pair of clauses about 'not restrained' (ese-ü buγsažu), the sentence on Ödchigin's sleeping and rising, and the dogs' list; the notes say where. The Mongol readings follow Shiratori; the English is a first drafting.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Teġün-dür Tajaṅ Qān kiliṅlažu ügülerün:

morph.gloss: that (oblique stem of tere) [那的 裏]
qan, sovereign (short form, after a name) [皇帝]
to be angry (stem inferred from the Ming) [怒着]

sentences.l: At that, Tajaṅ Qān being-angry, saying:
sentences.i: At this, Tayang Qan grew angry and said:
sentences.n: Teġün-dür is the oblique stem teġün (from tere 'that') with the dative-locative -dür, which the Ming reads 那的裏, 'at that'; I take it as 'thereupon'. kiliṅlažu 'being angry' is a converb in -žu (Ming 怒着, 着 being the Ming's mark of the converb); the stem kiliṅla- is inferred from that gloss. ügülerün (Ming 說) is a second converb, 'saying', and the colon opens the speech. Qān after a name is the short form of qaγan. Two converbs back to back is the pattern of the whole section: each speech is introduced 'X ügülerün:', 'X saying:'.

sentences.t: "Ükükü amin žoboqu beje bügüde nigen bijü-že.

morph.gloss: to die (stem inferred from the Ming) [死的]
to toil, suffer (stem inferred from the Ming 辛苦) [辛苦的]
to be (present form bijü) [有 也者︀]

sentences.l: "Dying life, toiling body: all one it-is indeed.
sentences.i: "A life that ends in death, a body that toils: all of it is one.
sentences.n: Hard to read: the Ming gives 死的 性命 辛苦的 身子 都 一 有也者, 'dying life, toilsome body, all one, it is indeed'. ükükü (死的) and žoboqu (辛苦的) are participles in -kü and -qu standing before the noun they describe; the stems ükü- 'die' and žobo- 'toil, suffer' are inferred from the Ming. bügüde nigen is 'all one' (都 一), and bijü-že is bü- 'be' with the assertion particle -že. I take the sense to be that life that ends in death and a body that labours come to the same, so there is nothing to be gained by waiting; that is my reading, not a translation I can check. The opening quotation mark is Shiratori's, and the speech is Tayang's.

sentences.t: Tein böġesü qadqulduja"

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀牙 qadqulduja

morph.gloss: to fight, strike (stem inferred from the Ming 殺) [厮殺︀咱]

sentences.l: So if-it-is, let-us-fight."
sentences.i: Then let us fight."
sentences.n: tein böġesü, 'so, if it be' (Ming 那般 有呵; 呵 is the Ming's mark of the conditional), is the standard 'in that case'. qadqulduja is the verb qadqu- 'fight, strike' (stem inferred from the Ming 殺, 'kill'), the reciprocal -ldu- 'one another' and the hortative -ja, 'let us' (Ming 咱 marks the first-person plural). The closing quotation mark ends Tayang's speech.

sentences.t: keġežü Qačir Usun-ača ködölžü Tamir huruγ̇u jabuγ̇ad

morph.gloss: to move, set out (stem inferred from the Ming 動) [動着]

sentences.l: Saying, from the Qačir water moving, the Tamir downstream having-gone,
sentences.i: So saying, he moved from the river Qachir and went down along the Tamir,
sentences.n: The first of five units (3-7) made from one long chain of converbs (keġežü … ködölžü … jabuγad … ketülžü … kürčü … üžežü … kürgeġesü … kürġeġülüġed … bolurun): Shiratori prints no stop until the colon at bolurun (there is none at aisai), so I have cut it at the natural joints and the English is a running sentence across them. Usun-ača is 'from the water' (Ming 水行, 'to the water'; the ablative -ača is what the sense needs here, so the Ming 行 is loose). huruγu (Ming 順) is 'following the course, downstream'; I take it as the adverb for Tamir. jabuγad is the converb 'having gone' (-γad), and I translate 'went down along' because the sentence goes on.

sentences.t: Orqon-i ketülžü Naqu γun-(n)u doronaži qormai daγ̇arin Čakirmaγ̇ud kürčü

morph.gloss: skirt, hem (here the foot of the mountain) [裙]
to pass along, go by [經過]

sentences.l: Orqon crossing, Naqu's cliff's east-side skirt passing-along, to Čakirmaγud having-arrived,
sentences.i: crossed the Orqon, passed along the skirt of the Naqu cliff on its east side, and came to Chakirma'ud;
sentences.n: Second link of the chain. Orqon-i has the accusative -i: the river is crossed, 'crossed the Orqon' (Ming 河名行). Naqu γun-(n)u is 'of the Naqu cliff' (Ming 山名 崖的), with the genitive -(n)u; the (n) is Shiratori's. doronaži: dorona 'east' (reading uncertain) with -ži 'toward, on the side'; the Ming 東邊 is 'east side', which I follow. qormai is the Ming 裙, 'skirt, hem', the foot of the cliff; daγarin is a converb from daγari- 'pass along' (Ming 經過). Čakirmaγud is glossed only 地名, 'place name'.

sentences.t: aisuqui-dur Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)u qaraγ̇ul üžežü

words.reading: 阿亦速中灰-突︀舌兒 aisuqui-dur

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title of Temüjin [太祖︀]

sentences.l: At the coming, Čiṅgis Qaγan's scout seeing,
sentences.i: and when he came there, Chinggis Qahan's scouts saw him,
sentences.n: aisuqui-dur is aisu- 'come', the participle -qui and the dative-locative -dur: 'at the coming, when (he) came' (Ming 來的時). The subject of the coming is the Naiman, as the next unit says, although here the English must read the sentence in one pass. Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)u qaraγul is 'Chinggis Qahan's scout'; qaraγul is singular in form and here evidently collective, hence "scouts". üžežü 'seeing' is a converb (Ming 見着), and the chain continues into the report.

sentences.t: Naiman kürčü aisai keġen kelen kürgeġesü

morph.gloss: to bring to, deliver (kür- 'reach' made causative; uncertain) [送到呵]

sentences.l: Naiman arriving come, saying word if-conveyed,
sentences.i: and reported: "The Naiman have arrived and are coming." When this word was delivered,
sentences.n: Naiman kürčü aisai keġen is the report, 'the Naiman, arriving, come', closed by keġen (Ming 麽道, the converb that shuts a quotation). Shiratori prints no quotation marks round it; I have put them in my English. aisai (Ming 來也) is 'is coming': the stem ai- is uncertain and I take -sai as the present ending. kürgeġesü is kürge- 'bring to, deliver' with the conditional -ġesü (Ming 送到呵, 'if it is sent'), i.e. 'when the word was delivered'.

sentences.t: ene kelen kürġeġülüġed Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:

words.reading: 古舌兒格兀魯額惕 kürġeġülüġed

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title of Temüjin [太祖︀]

sentences.l: This word having-caused-to-reach, Čiṅgis Qaγan, when decree making:
sentences.i: When this word had been brought, Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: kürġeġülüġed is the causative converb 'having caused to reach' (-ġül- causative, -üġed converb; Ming 被到了, 'was conveyed'). žarliγ bolurun 'when making a decree' (Ming 聖旨 做) is the house rendering 'issued a decree:'. The colon opens the speech; it is closed at bolumn-že in the next unit.

sentences.t: "olon-(n)ača olon čüġen-(n)eče čüġen qor bolumn-že"

morph.gloss: loss, damage (the Ming 折損; the same spelling as qor 'quiver', and I take it as a different word) [折損]

sentences.l: "From many many, from few few, loss it-becomes indeed."
sentences.i: "From the many, many; from the few, few: there will be loss."
sentences.n: Obscure. olon-(n)ača olon, čüġen-(n)eče čüġen is 'from many, many; from few, few' (Ming 多行多 少行少); the ablative is used for 'out of'. qor has the Ming 折損, 'to break, lose', so I read it as 'loss, damage' and not as the quiver qor of other passages (or of qortu in unit 70); bolumn-že is bol- 'become', a present ending I cannot place (-umn), and the assertion -že. My sense is that the loss will be in proportion to the numbers, but a Mongol reader may have taken it another way. The opening quotation mark is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: kēġed esergü an-u morilažu

morph.gloss: converb: having -ed (run together with the stem, long ē)
their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: Having-said, facing, their mounting-horse,
sentences.i: Having said this, they mounted to meet them,
sentences.n: kēġed is keġe- 'say' with -ġed, 'having said', the two merged in one long-vowel spelling (Ming 說了). esergü (迎着) is 'facing, to meet'; an-u 'their' (Ming 他的) is the third-person genitive set after its noun. morilažu is built on morin 'horse': morin + the verb-forming -la- + converb -žu, 'horse-ing', i.e. 'mounting' (Ming 上馬着). The subject is Chinggis's army, which is why I put 'they'; the Ming says only 他的, 'their'.

sentences.t: qaraγ̇ul-i an-u hüldeġed čerig žasarun:

morph.gloss: their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to arrange, put in order [整治時]

sentences.l: The scouts, theirs, having-chased, the army when arranging:
sentences.i: They chased off the enemy scouts, and as they drew up the army,
sentences.n: Ming 哨望的行 他的 趕了 軍 整治時: qaraγul-i is the accusative, 'the scouts'; an-u 'their' (the enemy's, i.e. the Naiman's); hüldeġed 'having chased'. žasarun is žasa- 'arrange, put in order' with -run 'when' (Ming 整治時). The colon marks that the order of battle follows. The Ming is clear on the words but not on who does what; the chaser is Chinggis's side.

sentences.t: "Qaraγana jorčil jorčižu

morph.gloss: thicket (Ming 叢草般, 'like a clump of grass') [叢草般]

sentences.l: "Qaraγana going, going,
sentences.i: "Advancing like a thicket,
sentences.n: Qaraγana is glossed 叢草般, 'like a clump of grass', so a thicket or bush; the Ming has no word for 'like', so it may sit in the ending. jorčil (Ming 行) and jorčižu (去着) are two forms of jorči- 'go, set out'. I read jorčil as a verbal form ending in -l that I cannot place. The opening quotation mark is Shiratori's. The three similes (thicket, lake, chisel) describe how the army moves, stands and strikes.

sentences.t: naγ̇ur baildu baildužu šiγ̇uči qadqulduγ̇a qadqulduja" keġeldübe.

words.reading: 中合(惕)中忽勒都︀阿 qadqulduγ̇a

morph.gloss: ending of uncertain force (optative or nominal), here 'in fighting'

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀牙 qadqulduja

morph.gloss: to fight, strike (stem inferred from the Ming 殺) [厮殺︀咱]

sentences.l: lake-like array standing, chisel-like fighting(-γa), let-us-fight", they-said-together.
sentences.i: standing in array like a lake and fighting like a chisel, let us fight!" they said together.
sentences.n: naγur 'lake' (Ming 海子, 'sea-child') is the simile for the standing line: baildu (Ming 陣, 'battle array') and baildužu, 'standing' (bai-, the reciprocal -ldu-, converb -žu). šiγuči (Ming 鑿子般) is the chisel, narrow and driving. qadqulduγa is the same verb as qadqulduja, but the Ming has no 咱 on it, so it is not the hortative; its -γa is of uncertain force (an optative or noun ending), and the two together read 'fighting, let us fight' (Ming 厮殺 / 厮殺咱). keġeldübe, 'said together' (Ming 共說了), closes the unit with the reciprocal -ldü-: the order was agreed by all.

sentences.t: Tein kēġed Čiṅgis Qaγan öġesün alginčilažu Qasar-i γol žasaγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: converb: having -ed (run together with the stem, long ē)
Chinggis, the title of Temüjin [太祖︀]
to act as vanguard (analysis uncertain) [頭做着]
centre, main body of an army [中軍]
to arrange, put in order [敎整治了]

sentences.l: So having-said, Čiṅgis Qaγan himself as-vanguard-acting, Qasar the main-body had-arranged.
sentences.i: Then Chinggis Qahan himself led the vanguard, and had Qasar arrange the main body.
sentences.n: alginčilažu is glossed 頭做着, 'making (himself) the head'; I take it as 'acting as vanguard' but the stem is a guess. öġesün is 'himself' (自己). Qasar-i has the accusative -i (Ming 人名行) and γol is 'centre, main body' (中軍); žasaγulba is žasa- 'arrange' with the causative -γul- and the past -ba (Ming 敎整治了, 'had it arranged'). So Qasar is the one who is made to arrange it; the English 'had Qasar arrange' follows the causative.

sentences.t: Ödčigin nojan-i kötöd žasaγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: (horse) led along, following (stem uncertain; compare kötöl in the glossary) [從馬(每)]
to arrange, put in order [敎整治了]

sentences.l: Ödčigin Noyan, the following-horses had-arranged.
sentences.i: He had Ödchigin Noyan arrange the reserve horses.
sentences.n: Same verb, žasaγulba, 'caused to arrange' (Ming 敎整治了). nojan-i is 'the noyan' with the accusative -i (Ming 官人行). kötöd is glossed 從馬(每), 'following horses', and I take it as a plural in -d of a stem kötö- (probably the led or spare horses); the stem is a guess (compare kötöl 'led, following' in the glossary), so 'reserve horses' is my interpretation of 'following'.

sentences.t: Naiman Čakirmaγ̇ud-ača ičužu Naqu γun-(n)u ebür aγ̇ula-jin qormai kižin baižuγ̇ui.

words.reading: 察乞舌兒馬兀荅察 Čakirmaγ̇ud-ača

morph.gloss: skirt, hem (here the foot of the mountain) [裙]
along, alongside (Ming 緣着; uncertain) [緣着]

sentences.l: Naiman from Čakirmaγud withdrawing, Naqu's cliff's front, the mountain's skirt along, stood.
sentences.i: The Naiman fell back from Chakirma'ud and took up position in front of the Naqu cliff, along the skirt of the mountain.
sentences.n: Čakirmaγud-ača is the ablative, 'from Chakirma'ud' (Ming 地名處). ičužu (Ming 退着) is 'drawing back': the stem ičü- is inferred. ebür is the Ming's 前, 'front, the near side', not the usual 'bosom'; aγula-jin is 'of the mountain' with -jin after a vowel; qormai 'skirt' is the same word as above; kižin (Ming 緣着, 'along') is a postposition I cannot place further. baižuγui (Ming 立了) is the perfect of bai-: 'stood, has stood'.

sentences.t: Tedüi Naiman-u qaraγ̇ul-i bidan-u qaraγ̇ul hüldeġed

morph.gloss: then, thereupon (Ming 卽便 'at once') [卽便]

sentences.l: Then, the Naiman's scouts our scouts having-chased,
sentences.i: Then our scouts chased the Naiman scouts
sentences.n: tedüi is 'then, thereupon' (Ming 卽便, 'at once'). Naiman-u qaraγul-i is 'the Naiman's scouts' as object (-i), bidan-u qaraγul 'our scouts', with bida 'we (inclusive)' in the genitive; hüldeġed 'having chased' (Ming 趕了). The sentence runs on into the next unit (the same chase continues to the Naiman main body), and I have cut it there.

sentences.t: Naqu γun-(n)u ebür jeke γol-dur an-u neiletele hüldeġed kürčüġüi.

morph.gloss: centre, main body of an army [中軍 裏]
their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: Naqu's cliff's front, great main-body-at, their joining, straight having-chased, arrived.
sentences.i: to the front of the Naqu cliff, and chased them straight on until they met the great main body of the Naiman.
sentences.n: Ming: 山名 崖的 前 大 中軍裏 他的 相合 直趕 到了. γol-dur is 'in the centre' (Ming 中軍裏); neiletele is neile- 'join, meet' with -tele 'right up to' (Ming 相合, 'together'), and hüldeġed 'having chased' (Ming 直趕, 'chase straight'). kürčüġüi is the perfect of kür- 'reach' (Ming 到了). The subject is our scouts; the Ming has only 'arrived', so I add nothing. Shiratori's full stop closes the sentence at kürčüġüi.

sentences.t: Tein hüldežü kürküi-ji Tajaṅ Qān üžežü

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (short form, after a name) [皇帝]

sentences.l: So chasing, the-arriving(acc.) Tajaṅ Qān seeing,
sentences.i: Tayang Qan saw them come chasing in this way,
sentences.n: Tein hüldežü kürküi-ji is Ming 那般 趕着 到的行: 'thus chasing, the arriving (one) as object'. kürküi-ji is kür- 'reach', the participle -küi and the accusative -ji (after a vowel): the participle is turned into an object, 'the one who is arriving'. Then üžežü 'seeing' (Ming 見着). I take the sense to be that Tayang sees our scouts arriving, chasing his own; the object is the pursuer. The tempting alternative, that the Naiman are the chasers, is ruled out by the preceding unit.

sentences.t: Žamuqa tende Naiman-luγ̇a čerig morilažu ireldüžü tende ažu

morph.gloss: the Naiman, a people [種名 一同]

sentences.l: Jamuqa there, with the Naiman, the army having-mounted, having-come-together, there staying,
sentences.i: Jamuqa was there: he had mounted with the Naiman army, come with them, and was staying there,
sentences.n: Jamuqa is the Mongol who has gone over to the Naiman. tende is 'there'; Naiman-luγa has the comitative -luγa, 'with the Naiman' (Ming 一同, 'together'); morilažu 'mounting' is built on morin 'horse' and ireldüžü 'coming together' on ire- 'come' with the reciprocal -ldü- (Ming 共來着). tende ažu 'there staying' (Ming 住着). So the unit says that Jamuqa is with the Naiman army at this place. The Ming is five converbs in a row; my English runs them together as clauses.

sentences.t: Tajaṅ Qān Žamuqa-dāča asaγčuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (short form, after a name) [皇帝]
Jamuqa, a man's name [人名 處]

sentences.l: Tajaṅ Qān from Žamuqa had-asked.
sentences.i: Tayang Qan asked Jamuqa:
sentences.n: Žamuqa-dāča has the ablative with a long vowel -dāča (Ming 人名處, 'at the person's place'): to ask 'from' someone is to ask him. asaγčuγu is asaγ- 'ask' with -čuγu, the past after a consonant (Ming 問有來, 'had asked'). The stop closes the sentence, but what follows is the content of the question, and the opening quotation mark is not printed; I supply it in my English.

sentences.t: Tede jaγ̇ud olon qonid čino hüldežü qoton-dur kürtele hüldežü irekü metü

morph.gloss: what, whichever (plural; Ming 甚麽每; uncertain) [甚麽每]
enclosure, pen (Ming 圈子) [圈子 裏]

sentences.l: Those, whatever, many sheep, a wolf having-chased, up-to-the-pen having-chased, coming like —
sentences.i: "Those, whoever they are, who come like a wolf driving many sheep right up to the pen —
sentences.n: Shiratori prints no opening quotation mark; the closing one is at aisai. tede jaγud is Ming 那的每 甚麽每, 'those whatever (ones)', an indefinite plural 'whoever they are'. olon qonid čino hüldežü: 'many sheep, a wolf chasing' (a wolf drives sheep), then qoton-dur kürtele 'right up to the pen' and hüldežü irekü metü 'chasing, like the coming'. metü (Ming 般) 'like' follows the participle irekü. I have kept the simile whole, though the wolf's part is the Ming's and the sentence is long.

sentences.t: ede jaγ̇ud haran tein hüldežü aisai" keġen asaγba.

morph.gloss: what, whichever (plural; Ming 甚麽每; uncertain) [甚麽每]

sentences.l: these whatever people thus chasing come" saying, he-asked.
sentences.i: who are these people that come driving in that way?" he asked.
sentences.n: ede jaγud haran is 'these, whatever, people' (Ming 這的每 甚麽每 人): ede is the plural of ene. tein hüldežü aisai 'thus chasing, come' (Ming 那般 趕着 來也). keġen asaγba 'saying, asked' (Ming 麽道 問了) is the way a quotation is closed: the converb keġen 'saying' shuts the quotation and the finite verb follows. The question is the same one begun in the previous unit; I cut the long sentence at the end of the simile.

sentences.t: Žamuqa ügülerün:
sentences.l: Žamuqa saying:
sentences.i: Jamuqa said:
sentences.n: A plain speech-introduction, Žamuqa ügülerün 'Jamuqa saying' (Ming 說); the colon opens his answer.

sentences.t: "Temüžin anda min-u dörben noγais-i

morph.gloss: my (bi, stem min-, + -u set after its noun) [我的]

sentences.l: "Temüžin, my anda, four dogs(acc.),
sentences.i: "My sworn brother Temüjin has four dogs,
sentences.n: Opening quotation mark printed at Temüžin. anda min-u is 'my anda' (Ming 契合 我的): anda is the sworn brother, min-u the genitive of bi 'I' set after its noun. dörben noγais-i is 'four dogs' with the accusative -i (Ming 四箇 狗行), the object of the verb in the next unit. Jamuqa speaks of his old anda, Temüjin, with the word that once bound them.

sentences.t: küġün-(n)ü miqa-γ̇ar težiġežü ginžiležü hujažu aqu büleġe.
sentences.l: man's with-flesh having-fed, having-chained, having-tied, kept there-were.
sentences.i: which he has fed on human flesh and kept bound with iron chains.
sentences.n: küġün-(n)ü miqa-γar is 'with a man's meat' (Ming 人的 肉敎): the genitive -(n)ü and the instrumental -γar. težiġežü is 'feeding, rearing' (養着), ginžiležü 'chaining' (ginži 'chain', Ming 鐵索, with -le-), hujažu 'binding, tying' (拴着); aqu büleġe (Ming 住 有來) is 'were, kept'. büleġe is the past 'there was'. I render büleġe with a perfect ('has fed … and kept'), since Jamuqa is describing what has been done to the dogs.

sentences.t: Tede qaraγ̇ul-i bidan-u hüldežü aisunqun tede bi-že.

morph.gloss: to be (stem bi- before -že) [有 也者︀]

sentences.l: Those, our scouts having-chased, the coming-ones, those are indeed.
sentences.i: Those who come chasing our scouts are those very dogs.
sentences.n: tede is the plural 'those'; 'the four dogs' in the English is understood from the previous sentence. qaraγul-i bidan-u hüldežü aisunqun: 'our scouts chasing, the coming ones'. aisunqun (Ming 來的每) is aisu- 'come' with the plural participle -nqun, 'those who come'. bi-že, 'it is indeed' (Ming 有), has the stem bi- (a short form of bü- 'be') and the assertion particle -že: no copula is needed in Mongol, but the stem is here, as in bijü-že above.

sentences.t: Tede dörben noγais širemün maṅlaitan
sentences.l: Those four dogs, raw-copper foreheads-having,
sentences.i: Those four dogs have foreheads of raw copper,
sentences.n: Ming 那的每 四箇 狗每 生銅 額顱有的(每). maṅlaitan is maṅlai 'forehead' (Ming 額顱) with -tan, the plural of the possessive (-tu/-tai), 'those having foreheads' (Ming 有的每); the glossary treats -ten the same way. The noun that describes goes before: širemün maṅlaitan, 'copper-foreheaded'. The Ming 生銅 is 'raw copper'. A series of five such compounds follows, one for each part of the dogs, so the structure is learned once.

sentences.t: šiγ̇uči qošiγ̇utan šibüge keleten temür öreten üldü minaγ̇atan

morph.gloss: beak, muzzle (Ming 觜) [觜 有的(每)]
whip (Ming 做鞭) [做鞭 有的(每)]

sentences.l: chisel mouths-having, awl tongues-having, iron hearts-having, ring-sword whips-having,
sentences.i: mouths of chisel, tongues of awl, hearts of iron, and ring-swords for whips,
sentences.n: The same pattern as the last unit: noun + possessive plural, here five nouns in a row. šiγuči qošiγutan, 'chisel (as) beak-having' (Ming 觜有的, 'with beaks'); šibüge keleten 'awl as tongue-having'; temür öreten 'iron as heart-having'; üldü minaγatan 'ring-sword as whip-having' (Ming 鐶刀 做鞭 有的). minaγa is glossed 做鞭, 'made into a whip'; the stem and its sense are my best reading. The English has to turn 'copper-foreheaded' into prepositional phrases to be read aloud.

sentences.t: šiġüderi idežü kei unužu jabud tede.
sentences.l: Dew eating, wind riding, going, those.
sentences.i: They feed on dew and ride the wind as they go.
sentences.n: šiġüderi is Ming 露, 'dew', with the accusative -i as the object of 'eating'; the stem šiġüder is not otherwise in the glossary, so I give it as a guess. idežü 'eating' and unužu 'riding' are converbs (Ming 喫着, 騎着); kei is 'wind'. jabud is jabu- 'go' with a plural ending -d (Ming 行每, 'those going'). The full stop at tede closes a sentence; the final tede resumes the subject and is not rendered separately.

sentences.t: Alalduqui üdür haran-u miqa ided tede.
sentences.l: Killing-each-other's day, people's flesh the-eaters, those.
sentences.i: On the day of killing one another, those eat men's flesh.
sentences.n: alalduqui is ala- 'kill', the reciprocal -ldu- and the participle -qui, 'of mutual killing' (Ming 厮殺的), before üdür 'day'. haran-u miqa is 'people's meat' (genitive -u); ided (Ming 喫每) is ide- 'eat' with a plural ending, 'those who eat'. The sentence is a general description of the dogs' diet; The final tede is the subject: 'those eat'.

sentences.t: Kürülčekü üdür küġün-ü miqa künesüled tede.

morph.gloss: provisions for a journey (Ming 行糧) [做行糧]

sentences.l: Meeting-each-other's day, man's flesh as-provisions, those.
sentences.i: On the day of meeting, those take men's flesh as their provisions.
sentences.n: kürülčekü is kür- 'reach' with a reciprocal (I read -ülče-; uncertain) and the participle -kü: 'the meeting each other' (Ming 相到的). küġün-ü miqa künesüled: 'man's meat, making into provisions' (Ming 古捏速列惕 做行糧): künesü is 'provisions for a journey', and the verb-forming -le- and plural -d give 'those who make it their provisions'. The final tede is again the subject. The balance with the last unit (killing days / meeting days) is Shiratori's punctuation, a pair of short sentences.

sentences.t: Ginži-ben mültüldežü edöġe ese-ü buγsažu aγsad

morph.gloss: iron chain (Ming 鐵索) [鐵索自的行]
to slip free, be pulled off (stem inferred from the Ming 被脫) [被脫着]
not (negative of the past; 'not yet' before a converb) [不曾 麽]
to restrain, tie up (Ming 拘束) [拘束着]
past participle plural: those who were

sentences.l: Own iron-chains having-slipped, now not(?) restrained being-ones,
sentences.i: They have slipped their iron chains; now, unrestrained,
sentences.n: Hard. ginži-ben is 'own iron chain' with the reflexive-possessive -ben (Ming 鐵索自的行). mültüldežü (Ming 被脫着, 'being slipped off') is a passive converb whose stem I infer. edöġe is 'now' (Ming 如今); then ese-ü buγsažu aγsad, glossed 不曾麽 拘束着 有的每, 'not-yet? restrained, those who were'. ese is 'not' (of the past; the glossary has 'not yet' before a converb), -ü is the particle the Ming renders 麽 (a question or emphasis; uncertain), buγsažu 'restraining' (拘束) and aγsad 'those who were': so 'those not (yet) restrained', which agrees with the dogs having slipped their chains. The negative is therefore rendered as 'unrestrained'. The same ese-ü stands after edöġe in the unit 48; there the Ming 不曾麽 sits before bajasču 'rejoicing' and the negative does not fit the sense, so it is left unrendered. The split is doubtful and the glosser should not trust it.

sentences.t: bajasču tein šilemelčen aisai tede" keġežüġüi.

morph.gloss: to drool, to covet (Ming 垂涎) [垂涎着]

sentences.l: Rejoicing, so drooling coming those" having-said.
sentences.i: rejoice and come drooling in that way," he said.
sentences.n: bajasču is bajas- 'rejoice' (Ming 喜歡着), the converb -ču. šilemelčen (Ming 垂涎着) is 'drooling, coveting', converb in -n, a stem šilemelče-; aisai tede 'they come, those'. The closing quotation mark is at tede, and keġežüġüi (Ming 說了) 'he said' follows: -žüġüi is the past of keġe- with the front-vowel form of -žuγui. Jamuqa's description of Chinggis's four officers as hounds is complete.

sentences.t: "Tede dörben noγais ked tede kēġesü

morph.gloss: who (plural; read from the Ming 誰每; uncertain) [誰每]
conditional: if one says (run together with the stem, long ē)

sentences.l: "Those four dogs, who those, if one say:
sentences.i: "If you ask who those four dogs are:
sentences.n: A fresh quotation mark at Tede; the speaker is not marked, and I take it as Jamuqa still, the first part is his conditional: tede dörben noγais ked tede kēġesü, Ming 那的每 四箇 狗每 誰每 那的每 說呵, 'those four dogs, who those, if (you) say'. ked 'who (plural)' is read from the Ming 誰每 and is uncertain. kēġesü is keġe- 'say' with the conditional -ġesü, the two run together in the long-vowel spelling (as in kēġed). The question is rhetorical: Jamuqa asks it himself and answers it in the next unit.

sentences.t: Žebe, Qubilai qojar Želme, Sübeġetei qojar tede dörben bi" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Žebe, Qubilai two, Želme, Sübeġetei two, those four are" he-said.
sentences.i: Jebe and Qubilai, the two; Jelme and Sübegetei, the two: those four they are," he said.
sentences.n: Žebe Qubilai qojar, 'Jebe, Qubilai, two' (Ming 兩箇): qojar 'two' follows the pair it counts. Želme Sübeġetei qojar likewise. tede dörben bi: 'those four are', with bi (Ming 有) the short form of bü- 'be'. Names: Jebe, Qubilai, Jelme and Sübegetei are the four officers (the 'four hounds') of Chinggis. The closing quotation mark is at bi, and keġežüġüi 'he said' closes the speech.

sentences.t: Tajaṅ Qān ügülerün:

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (short form, after a name) [皇帝]

sentences.l: Tajaṅ Qān saying:
sentences.i: Tayang Qan said:
sentences.n: As before, ügülerün 'saying' with the colon; the next unit is Tayang's speech.

sentences.t: "Ele tede doromži-ača qolo baija"

morph.gloss: lowly, inferior (Ming 下等) [下等 處]

sentences.l: "Only those from the lowly far let-us-stand"
sentences.i: "Let us keep far away from those lowly ones"
sentences.n: ele (Ming 但, 'only') is an emphatic particle whose force is unsettled. tede doromži-ača qolo baija: 'from those lowly (ones), far, let us stand'. doromži (Ming 下等) is 'inferior, lowly' with the ablative -ača, and the Ming 處 could mean the place or the persons; I read persons. baija is bai- 'stand' with the hortative -ja (Ming 立咱, 咱 'we'). So 'keep far from' for 'stand far from'.

sentences.t: keġežü qoinaγši iqurižu aγ̇ula asan baiba.

morph.gloss: to move, shift (Ming 挪; stem inferred) [挪着]
carrying on the back or shoulder (Ming 擔 'to carry'; not the name Asan; stem uncertain) [擔]

sentences.l: saying, backward having-moved, mountain carrying stood.
sentences.i: and so saying he moved back and stood with the mountain at his back.
sentences.n: keġežü 'saying' is the converb (Ming 說着); qoinaγši is 'toward behind' (Ming 往後) and iqurižu 'moving' (挪着, the stem iquri- inferred). aγula asan baiba: 'mountain' + asan (Ming 擔, 'to carry on the shoulder or back') + baiba 'stood'. asan is not the name Asan as in the glossary; I take it as 'carrying' and the phrase as 'with the mountain on his back'. This is a guess at an obscure image, though the Ming 擔 is clear.

sentences.t: Teġün-ü qoināča dujalžu toγ̇oriγažu aisqun-i:

morph.gloss: to leap, exult (Ming 歡躍) [歡躍着]

sentences.l: Of-that behind-from rejoicing, circling, the coming-ones
sentences.i: Those who came up behind them, leaping about and circling round —
sentences.n: teġün-ü qoināča: 'from behind of that' (Ming 那的 後行): teġün-ü is the genitive of tere, 'their', qoināča 'from behind'. dujalžu 'rejoicing, leaping' (歡躍着) and toγoriγažu 'circling' (繞着) are converbs; aisqun-i is 'the coming ones' with the accusative -i (來的每行). The colon at the end of the unit marks the point where Tayang's seeing and asking begin in the next; it is a long sentence of which the object comes before the verb 'seeing'.

sentences.t: üžežü basa Tajaṅ Qān Žamuqa-dāča asaγčuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (short form, after a name) [皇帝]
Jamuqa, a man's name [人名 處]

sentences.l: seeing, again Tajaṅ Qān from Žamuqa had-asked.
sentences.i: Tayang Qan saw them, and asked Jamuqa again:
sentences.n: üžežü 'seeing' (見着) governs the object of the last unit: Tayang, having seen the ones coming, asked. basa is 'again' (再). asaγčuγu is 'had asked' (the -čuγu form after a consonant stem, as in the ask above). The question is in the next unit.

sentences.t: Tede jaγ̇ud erte talbiγsad unuγan eke-jüġen sün kököžü

morph.gloss: what, whichever (plural; Ming 甚麽每; uncertain) [甚麽每]
to set down, let loose [放了的(每)]
past participle plural: those that were
to suck (Ming 咂; stem inferred) [咂着]

sentences.l: Those, whatever, early set-loose foals own-mother milk sucking,
sentences.i: "Those, whatever, like foals that were let loose early and suck milk from their own mothers,
sentences.n: No opening quotation mark in the print. tede jaγud: 'those, whatever'; erte talbiγsad unuγan: 'early, set-loose, foals' (Ming 早 放了的 駒兒), with talbiγsad the past participle plural (-γsad) 'those that were released', here describing foals. eke-jüġen is 'their own mother' with the reflexive-possessive -jüġen (Ming 母自的行; the 行 marks an oblique case, so 'from' is the sense of the verb), sün kököžü 'milk sucking' (Ming 乳 咂着). The comparison metü comes in the next unit.

sentences.t: eke-jüġen horčin torolun güjikü unuγad metü

morph.gloss: nimbly, swiftly (Ming 疾靈; stem uncertain) [疾靈]
to run (Ming 走; stem inferred) [走的]

sentences.l: own-mother around nimbly running foals like,
sentences.i: run swiftly around their own mothers,
sentences.n: eke-jüġen horčin is 'around one's own mother' (Ming 母自的行 周圍). torolun is glossed 疾靈, 'swift, quick', and I cannot place the stem; güjikü is 'the running (ones)' (走的, stem güji- inferred), unuγad 'foals' (駒兒每) and metü 'like' (般), as in the foals simile of the earlier unit. I have joined torolun to the verb as an adverb, 'swiftly'; there is no way to check the stem.

sentences.t: jakin tein toγ̇oriγan aisai tede" keġen asaγčuγ̇u.
sentences.l: how thus circling come those" saying, he-had-asked.
sentences.i: why do they come circling in this way?" he asked.
sentences.n: jakin (Ming 如何) is 'how, why'. tein toγoriγan aisai tede: 'thus circling come, those' (那般 繞着 來也 那的每); toγoriγan is a converb in -n. keġen asaγčuγu 'saying, had asked' (麽道 問有來) closes the quotation, as before. The Ming 如何 could be read as either how or why, and I take 'why' for a question about behaviour; the Ming does not decide.

sentences.t: Žamuqa ügülerün:
sentences.l: Žamuqa saying:
sentences.i: Jamuqa said:
sentences.n: Plain speech-introduction, again.

sentences.t: "Tede židatu ere-ji žiγ̇užu čisutu tonoγ tonoγčin

morph.gloss: spear, lance (Ming 鎗) [鎗 有的]
to drive (Ming 趕; stem uncertain) [趕着]
blood (the n drops before -tu) [血 有的]

sentences.l: "Those spear-having men having-driven, blood-having strippers, strippers,
sentences.i: "Those who drive spear-bearing men, bloody strippers, strippers,
sentences.n: Opening quotation mark at Tede. tede židatu ere-ji žiγužu, Ming 那的每 鎗有的 男子行 趕着: 'those, spear-having man (accusative), driving'; židatu is žida 'spear' with possessive -tu. čisutu tonoγ tonoγčin: 'blood-having (adj) stripping, strippers' (Ming 血有的 剝脫 (剝脫的)每); the -čin is the 'one who does' ending. The compound is long and every part of it is my reading; the verb 'drive' (趕着) is from žiγu- whose stem I am unsure of.

sentences.t: üldütü ere-ji hüldežü unaγažu alažu üb tonaγ abuγčin

morph.gloss: stripping (variant of tonoγ; Ming 剝脫) [剝脫]

sentences.l: sword-having men having-chased, having-felled, having-killed, goods stripping-taking ones,
sentences.i: who chase sword-bearing men, cut them down and kill them, and strip and take their goods,
sentences.n: The parallel half: üldütü ere-ji hüldežü unaγažu alažu, 'sword-having man chasing, felling, killing' (Ming 刀有的 男子行 趕着 砍倒着 殺着), then üb tonaγ abuγčin, 'goods stripping taking ones' (Ming 財物 剝脫 要的每). unaγažu is una- 'fall' with the causative -γa-, 'to fell'. abuγčin is abu- 'take' with the agent ending -γčin. tonaγ is a variant of tonoγ.

sentences.t: Uruγ̇ud, Moṅγud keġegded tede.

morph.gloss: the Uruqud, a clan name [種名]
the Mongqud, a clan name [種名]

sentences.l: Uruγud, Moṅγud being-called, those.
sentences.i: are called the Uruqud and the Mongqud.
sentences.n: Uruγud (Uruqud, Ming 種名) and Moṅγud are clan names and take the plural -d. keġegded is keġe- 'say', the passive -gde- 'be called' and plural -d, 'those called' (Ming 被說的每). The sense is that the dog-like 'strippers' described are the clans of the Uruqud and the Mongqud: the Ming has no other word, and the 'those' tede closes with the full stop. Jamuqa has just named the four officers; this is a further description of the strippers, and who exactly he is pointing at is not clear to me.

sentences.t: Edöġe ese-ü bajasču tein dujalun aisai tede" keġežüġü.

morph.gloss: not (negative of the past) [不曾 麽]

sentences.l: Now not-(?) rejoicing, so leaping, come those" he-said.
sentences.i: Now they are glad and come leaping in that way," he said.
sentences.n: Edöġe is 'now' (Ming 如今); ese-ü, as above in this section, is glossed 不曾麽, 'not-yet?', and the 'not' does not fit the sense, so I have left it unrendered again, which is a doubt: here the Ming 不曾麽 could be a rhetorical question ("have they not rejoiced?") or an idiom with edöġe, "now at last"; I cannot decide, and the English gives only the plain sense that fits. bajasču 'rejoicing', tein 'so', dujalun 'leaping' (Ming 歡躍), aisai 'come'. The quotation closes at tede, and keġežüġü (Ming 說有, 'said') ends the speech: -žüġü is the narrative past.

sentences.t: Tendēče Tajaṅ Qān ügülerün:

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (short form, after a name) [皇帝]

sentences.l: From there Tajaṅ Qān saying:
sentences.i: At that, Tayang Qan said:
sentences.n: Tendēče is tende 'there' with the long-vowel ablative -ēče, 'from there' (Ming 自那裏): a narrative link, 'thereupon'.

sentences.t: "Ele tein böġesü tede doromži-ača qolo baija"

morph.gloss: lowly, inferior (Ming 下等) [下等每 行]

sentences.l: "Only so if-it-is, those from lowly ones far let-us-stand"
sentences.i: "If that is so, let us keep far from those lowly ones"
sentences.n: ele tein böġesü 'only so, if it is' (Ming 但 那般 有呵): the particle ele with the conditional böġesü is 'if only it be so'. The rest is the same phrase as in the earlier speech, tede doromži-ača qolo baija. The Ming here glosses doromži-ača 下等每 行, 'the lowly ones' (plural), which supports reading persons, not places.

sentences.t: keġežü basa qoinaγši aγ̇ula abarin baiba.

morph.gloss: to climb (Ming 登; stem inferred) [登]

sentences.l: saying, again backward mountain climbing stood.
sentences.i: and so saying he drew back again and climbed a mountain and stood.
sentences.n: keġežü, basa 'again', qoinaγši 'backward', aγula abarin 'mountain climbing' (Ming 山 登), baiba 'stood'. abarin is a converb of abari- 'climb' (Ming 登; stem inferred). The same movement as the earlier retreat (qoinaγši … aγula … baiba), but higher; the Ming repeats the phrase, and so do I.

sentences.t: Teġün-ü qoināča aisunqun öjesegsen šibaγ̇un metü šilemelčežü

morph.gloss: to be greedy, to crave (Ming 貪食; stem inferred) [貪食的]
bird (here a hawk; Ming 鷹) [鷹]

sentences.l: Of-that from-behind coming greedy hawk like, drooling,
sentences.i: "Those who come from behind them, drooling like a ravenous hawk
sentences.n: teġün-ü qoināča 'from behind of that' (Ming 那的 後行); aisunqun 'the coming ones'; öjesegsen šibaγun metü: 'greedy hawk like' (Ming 貪食的 鷹 般), where öjesegsen is a past participle used as 'the greedy' (the stem öjese- is inferred); šilemelčežü 'drooling' (垂涎着). The opening quotation mark is missing here too; only the close is printed, at bijü.

sentences.t: qušiγ̇uražu aisqun ken bijü" keġen Tajaṅ Qān Žamuqa-dāča asaγčuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: to stick out the tip (Ming 出尖; stem inferred) [出尖着]
qan, sovereign (short form, after a name) [皇帝]
Jamuqa, a man's name [人名 處]

sentences.l: beak-sticking-out, coming, who is" saying, Tajaṅ Qān from Žamuqa had-asked.
sentences.i: with their beaks stuck out, who are they?" asked Tayang Qan of Jamuqa.
sentences.n: qušiγuražu is 'sticking out the tip' (Ming 出尖着), the stem inferred from qušiγu 'beak' (perhaps the same word as qošiγu in qošiγutan above). aisqun ken bijü: 'the coming ones, who are they' (Ming 來的 誰 有), with bijü the present of bü- 'be'. keġen asaγčuγu 'saying, had asked' as before. The question is not marked at the start in the print, and I have supplied the quotation mark in the English.

sentences.t: Žamuqa ügülerün:
sentences.l: Žamuqa saying:
sentences.i: Jamuqa said:
sentences.n: Speech-introduction again, with the colon.

sentences.t: "Ene aisqu Temüžin anda min-u.

morph.gloss: my (bi, stem min-, + -u set after its noun) [我的]

sentences.l: "This coming Temüžin anda my.
sentences.i: "The one who is coming is my sworn brother Temüjin.
sentences.n: Opening quotation mark at Ene. ene aisqu is 'this one coming' (Ming 這 來的), with aisqu the participle of aisu- 'come'. Temüžin anda min-u: 'Temüjin, my anda' (Ming 契合 我的). min-u here is placed after anda as in the earlier speech, and the stop closes the sentence: 'this coming one is my sworn brother'.

sentences.t: Kübčin beje in-ü širemü-ġer širegdegsen šibüge-de qadququj-a čölö ügeiġü

morph.gloss: his, her (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to be smelted, forged (Ming 煉來; stem uncertain) [煉來的]

words.reading: 中合惕中忽中忽牙 qadququj-a

morph.gloss: gap, opening, free space (Ming 空隙) [空隙]

sentences.l: Whole his body with-raw-copper smelted awl-at to-the-stabbing gap there-is-none;
sentences.i: His whole body is smelted of raw copper: where an awl is stabbed, there is no gap;
sentences.n: Kübčin beje in-ü is 'the whole body of him' (全 身 他的), with in-ü the genitive 'his' placed after the noun. širemü-ġer širegdegsen: 'with copper (instrumental -ġer) smelted' (Ming 敎生銅 煉來的), where širegdegsen is a past participle of a verb I infer, širegde- 'be smelted'. šibüge-de qadququj-a čölö ügeiġü: 'to the awl, to the stabbing, gap none' (Ming 錐子行 刺的行 空隙 無的). qadququj-a is the participle qadqu-qu with a dative ending -(j)a; the -j- is a linking sound, I think. The unit means that the awl cannot find a place to enter.

sentences.t: temür(i)-jer dabtaγsan tebene-de qadququj-a čölö ügeiġü

morph.gloss: instrumental: with, of (after the omitted i)
to fold, to layer (Ming 疊) [疊到的]

words.reading: 中合惕中忽中忽牙 qadququj-a

morph.gloss: gap, opening, free space (Ming 空隙) [空隙]

sentences.l: with-iron layered, large-needle-at to-the-stabbing gap there-is-none.
sentences.i: he is layered with iron: where a big needle is stabbed, there is no gap.
sentences.n: The second half of the same image: temür(i)-jer is 'with iron' (instrumental -jer after the omitted i; Ming 鐵敎), dabtaγsan 'layered, folded' (Ming 疊到的), tebene-de 'to the big needle' (Ming 大針行), then the same refrain qadququj-a čölö ügeiġü. 'big needle' is Ming 大針; the Mongol tebene is a large needle. The two halves are a pair, both closed by the same words, so the parallelism is itself the lesson.

sentences.t: Temüžin anda min-u öjesegsen šibaγ̇un metü ein šilemelčen aisu-lu Üžebe-jüġü ta.

morph.gloss: my (bi, stem min-, + -u set after its noun) [我的]
to be greedy, to crave (Ming 貪食; stem inferred) [貪食的]
bird (here a hawk; Ming 鷹) [鷹]
to drool, to covet (Ming 垂涎) [垂涎]

sentences.l: Temüžin anda my greedy hawk like, thus drooling coming-indeed, have-you-seen, you.
sentences.i: My sworn brother Temüjin comes thus, drooling like a ravenous hawk: have you seen him?
sentences.n: Temüžin anda min-u as before; öjesegsen šibaγun metü 'like a greedy hawk' as in the earlier unit. ein šilemelčen aisu-lu: 'thus drooling, coming-' with -lu an ending I cannot place (Ming 來有 但, 'there is coming only'). Üžebe-jüġü ta: 'have (you) seen', the past -be and a question particle -jüġü (Ming 見了麽, 'have you seen?'), then ta 'you (plural, polite)'. The question is a rhetorical one that opens the warning that follows.

sentences.t: Naiman nököd Monγol-i üžeġesü ešige-jin γodu ülü hüleġülküi-eče büleġei;

morph.gloss: young ram, lamb (Ming 小羖) [小羖的]
to leave over, spare (Ming 剩下; stem inferred) [剩下的 行]

sentences.l: Naiman companions Mongols if-seeing, young-ram's hoof-skin not from-the-left-over there-was;
sentences.i: If the Naiman companions see the Mongols, there is not so much as a lamb's hoof left over;
sentences.n: Naiman nököd Monγol-i üžeġesü, 'the Naiman companions, if (they) see the Mongols' (Ming 乃蠻 伴當每 達達行 見呵; 'Tatars' is the Ming for Mongols). ešige-jin γodu ülü hüleġülküi-eče büleġei: 'of a young ram, hoof-skin, not, from the left-over, there was' (Ming 小羖的 蹄皮 不 剩下的行 有來). The negative ülü stands before the ablative and the verb büleġei closes the clause, so the sense is 'no hoof-skin of a lamb was among what is left'. büleġei is a past form (Ming 有來) in a speech about what happens whenever the Mongols meet the Naiman; I read it as the habitual result and put it in the present. nököd is left as 'companions'; whether it is a title of address or a description is not clear to me.

sentences.t: ta üžedkün" keġebe.
sentences.l: you look!" he-said.
sentences.i: Look, all of you!" he said.
sentences.n: ta üžedkün: 'you, look!' (Ming 您 看您), the ending -dkün being an imperative plural by the Ming's gloss. keġebe 'said' (Ming 說了). The closing quotation mark is at üžedkün; the speech began at Ene in unit 55.

sentences.t: Ene üge-dür Tajaṅ Qān ügülerün:

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (short form, after a name) [皇帝]

sentences.l: This in-word, Tajaṅ Qān saying:
sentences.i: At these words Tayang Qan said:
sentences.n: Ene üge-dür is 'in this word' (Ming 這 言語裏): üge 'word' with the dative-locative -dür, here 'at these words'. Then Tajaṅ Qān ügülerün 'saying', as before.

sentences.t: "Ele amsaγ̇ari aγ̇ula abarin baija"

morph.gloss: fearful, to be feared (Ming 可懼; ending uncertain) [可懼]
to climb (Ming 登; stem inferred) [登]

sentences.l: "Only fearful, mountain climbing let-us-stand"
sentences.i: "It is fearful; let us climb the mountain and stand,"
sentences.n: ele amsaγari (Ming 但 可懼): amsaγari is glossed 可懼, 'fearful', in a form I cannot analyse; it looks like an adverb or an exclamation. aγula abarin baija: 'mountain climbing, let us stand' (Ming 山 登 立咱). The Ming and the structure agree; the first half is the doubtful one. The quotation mark opens at Ele.

sentences.t: keġežü aγ̇ula abarižu baižuγ̇u.
sentences.l: saying, mountain having-climbed stood.
sentences.i: So saying, he climbed the mountain and stood there.
sentences.n: keġežü 'saying' and aγula abarižu 'having climbed the mountain' (Ming 登着), then baižuγu (Ming 立了有), the past of bai-. This is the third time the Ming records Tayang's retreat uphill (after units 38 and 51), each time a step higher, and each time the verb bai- 'stand' ends the unit; the chronicle uses it as a refrain of his fear.

sentences.t: Basa Tajaṅ Qān Žamuqa-dāča asaγurun:

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (short form, after a name) [皇帝]
Jamuqa, a man's name [人名 處]

sentences.l: Again Tajaṅ Qān from Žamuqa when-asking:
sentences.i: Again Tayang Qan asked Jamuqa:
sentences.n: Basa 'again' (再) and asaγurun, 'when asking' (Ming 問時): the converb in -urun 'when -ing', the same as in ügülerün and bolurun. The colon introduces the question.

sentences.t: "Basa tere qoināča žužaγ̇an-a aisunqun ken bijü" keġen asaγba.
sentences.l: "Again that from-behind thick-in coming who is" saying, he-asked.
sentences.i: "And who are those who come in a dense mass behind them?" he asked.
sentences.n: Basa tere qoināča žužaγan-a aisunqun ken bijü: 'again, that, from behind, thick(ly), the coming ones, who are' (Ming 再 那 後行 厚行 來的 誰 有). žužaγan is 'thick' (Ming 厚) with a dative -a, which I take as 'densely'. keġen asaγba 'saying, asked'. Shiratori prints no quotation mark at the beginning; the closing one is at bijü.

sentences.t: Žamuqa ügülerün:
sentences.l: Žamuqa saying:
sentences.i: Jamuqa said:
sentences.n: Speech-introduction. The quotation mark is opened in the next unit, at Höġelün.

sentences.t: "Höġelün eke nigen köġü-ben küġün-ü miqa-bar težiġežü büleġe.

morph.gloss: son (short form of köġün) [子 自的行]

sentences.l: "Höġelün mother one son-own, men's flesh with having-fed, had-been.
sentences.i: "Mother Högelün had one son, and she had fed him on human flesh.
sentences.n: Höġelün eke nigen köġü-ben: 'Högelün, mother, one son-own' (Ming 母名 母 一箇 子自的行), with köġü a short form of köġün 'son' and the reflexive-possessive -ben. küġün-ü miqa-bar težiġežü büleġe: 'with men's flesh feeding, was' (Ming 人的 肉教 養着 有來), where -bar is the instrumental. The reflexive -ben refers back to the subject of the clause, Högelün, so 'her own son' is right (Ming 子自的行); the English 'one son' keeps nigen. The 'he' of the next sentences is that son, called Jüchi-Qasar.

sentences.t: Γurban alda bejetü γunažin bodo idešitü

morph.gloss: three-year-old (Ming 三歲; analysis uncertain) [三歲]
head of livestock, animal (Ming 頭口) [頭口]

sentences.l: Three fathoms bodied, three-year animal food-having,
sentences.i: He is three fathoms in body, and eats a three-year-old beast as a meal,
sentences.n: γurban alda bejetü, 'three fathoms body-having' (Ming 三 度 身有的): alda is the fathom, the span of both arms; bejetü is beje 'body' with the possessive -tü. γunažin bodo idešitü 'three-year-old animal food-having' (Ming 三歲 頭口 喫食有的), where γunažin is a three-year-old (analysis uncertain), bodo a head of livestock and idešitü 'having a meal', from ide- 'eat'. The portrait of the giant begins with these possessives, as in the dogs.

sentences.t: γurban dabqur qujaγ emüsčü γurban buqa židgüġülžü aisu-že.

morph.gloss: armour, coat of mail (Ming 甲) [甲]
to drag, pull (Ming 拽; stem uncertain) [拽着]

sentences.l: three layers armour having-worn, three bulls having-caused-to-drag, comes indeed.
sentences.i: wears armour in three layers, drags three strong bulls behind him, and comes.
sentences.n: γurban dabqur qujaγ emüsčü: 'three layers armour, wearing' (Ming 三 層 甲 穿着). γurban buqa židgüġülžü: 'three bulls dragging' (Ming 三箇 强牛 拽着), with židgü- 'drag' and the causative -ġül- (so 'making drag, hauling'). aisu-že 'comes indeed' (Ming 來也者), the assertion -že. The quotation does not close here, since Jamuqa goes on in the next unit.

sentences.t: Qortu küġün-i qotola-ji žalgiγ̇asu qoγ̇olai-dur(i)-jan ülü tordaju;

morph.gloss: quiver (Ming 帶弓箭的 'bow-and-arrow-bearing') [帶弓箭的]

words.reading: 中豁斡來-都︀舌里-顏 qoγ̇olai-dur(i)-jan

morph.gloss: throat (Ming 喉嚨) [喉嚨 自的行]
to be hindered, to catch (Ming 被碍着; stem uncertain) [被碍着]

sentences.l: Quiver-having man entire if-swallowing, own-throat-in not is-caught;
sentences.i: If he swallows a whole man with his bow and quiver, it does not catch in his throat;
sentences.n: Qortu küġün-i qotola-ji: 'quiver-having man, entire' (Ming 帶弓箭的 人行 都行); qor 'quiver' with the possessive -tu here has the sense the Ming gives ('bow-and-arrow bearing') and is unlike the earlier qor 'loss' (Ming 折損). žalgiγasu is 'if (he) swallows' with the conditional -γasu (Ming 嚥呵). qoγolai-dur(i)-jan 'in his own throat' (Ming 喉嚨自的行), with the reflexive -(i)jan: the printed (i) is Shiratori's. ülü tordaju 'does not catch' (Ming 不 被碍着), with torda- 'be hindered' (stem uncertain).

sentences.t: kübčin ere-ji emküġesu öre ülü žasaju.

morph.gloss: to gulp down (Ming 呑; stem inferred) [呑呵]
to arrange, set right (Ming 點 'tick off'; sense uncertain) [點有]

sentences.l: whole man if-gulping, heart not sets-in-order.
sentences.i: if he gulps down a whole man, his heart is not eased.
sentences.n: kübčin ere-ji emküġesu, 'whole man, if (he) gulps' (Ming 全 男子行 呑呵); öre ülü žasaju, 'heart not (arranged)' (Ming 心 不 點有). žasa- is 'arrange, put in order' and the Ming 點 means to count, check off or touch lightly; so 'his heart is not even touched/eased' is a guess at an idiom. The sense (whole men are not enough to satisfy him) seems clear from the pair of clauses, but the last word is not.

sentences.t: Aγ̇urlaγ̇asu aṅγuγ̇a sumu-ban deližü talbiγ̇asu

morph.gloss: Angqu'a, the name of an arrow [箭名]
to draw (a bow) (Ming 拽; stem uncertain) [拽着]

sentences.l: Angry if, Aṅγuγa arrow-own having-drawn if-loosing,
sentences.i: If he is angered, he draws his own arrow Angqu'a and looses it,
sentences.n: aγurlaγasu 'if (he) is angry' (Ming 怒呵), then aṅγuγa (Ming 箭名, 'arrow name') sumu-ban 'own arrow', with the reflexive -ban. deližü 'drawing' (Ming 拽着) and talbiγasu 'if (he) lets go' (放呵). A series of conditionals in -γasu follows, each describing what the archer does and what results; the shot is described in the next unit.

sentences.t: aγ̇ula alus bükün harban qorin haran-i ülgetele qarbuju.

morph.gloss: passing beyond, across (Ming 越過) [越過]
to pierce through (Ming 直穿; stem inferred) [直穿了]

sentences.l: mountain beyond being, ten, twenty people through-and-through, he-shoots.
sentences.i: and he shoots through ten or twenty people beyond the mountain, right through them.
sentences.n: aγula alus bükün: 'beyond the mountain, being (ones)' (Ming 山 越過 有的), with bükün a participle plural of bü- 'be' (uncertain). harban qorin haran-i: 'ten, twenty people' (accusative -i; Ming 十箇 二十箇 人行). ülgetele 'right through' (Ming 直穿了), qarbuju 'shoots' (Ming 射有). The sense is clear: one arrow goes through the ones beyond the mountain, which is the point of the boast; 'beyond' is from alus (Ming 越過).

sentences.t: Kereldügsen nökör-i keġer ketüs bükün-i

morph.gloss: to fight one another (Ming 相鬪) [相鬪的]
open country, steppe (Ming 曠野) [曠野]
to cross over (Ming 渡過); the ending -s is uncertain [渡過]

sentences.l: Fighting-each-other companions open-country having-crossed being ones,
sentences.i: Companions fighting one another, who are across the open country,
sentences.n: Kereldügsen nökör-i keġer ketüs bükün-i: 'fighting-each-other companions (accusative), open country, crossing, being ones' (Ming 相鬪的 伴當行 曠野 渡過 有的行). kereldügsen is a past participle (stem kereldü- is a guess) and ketüs 'having crossed' (the ending is uncertain). This and the next unit give a second and bigger shot.

sentences.t: Keibür sumu-ban deližü talbiγ̇asu kelkitele ülketele qarbuju.

morph.gloss: Keibür, the name of an arrow [箭名]
to draw (a bow) (Ming 拽; stem uncertain) [拽着]
to link up, join (Ming 直連; stem inferred) [直連了]
to pierce through (variant spelling of ülgetele) [直穿了]

sentences.l: Keibür arrow-own having-drawn if-loosing, straight-linked, straight-through, he-shoots.
sentences.i: he draws his own arrow Keibür, looses it, and pierces them all through, one after another.
sentences.n: Keibür (Ming 箭名) is another named arrow. kelkitele is glossed 直連了, 'straight linked', and I read it as 'one after another in a line' (stem kelki- inferred); ülketele (兀勒客帖列) is a spelling variant of ülgetele, 'right through'. qarbuju 'shoots' (射有). Both shots hit people at a distance: the first the people beyond a mountain, the second people across open country.

sentences.t: Jekede deližü qarbuγ̇asu jesün žaγ̇ud alda γažar-a qarbuju;

morph.gloss: to draw (a bow) (Ming 拽; stem uncertain) [拽着]

sentences.l: Greatly having-drawn if-shooting, nine hundred fathoms ground-over he-shoots;
sentences.i: Drawn to the full and shot, it flies nine hundred fathoms over the ground;
sentences.n: jekede is jeke 'great' with the dative-locative -de, used as an adverb (Ming 大行): 'greatly, at full stretch'. deližü 'drawing', qarbuγasu 'if (he) shoots'; jesün žaγud alda γažar-a, 'nine hundred fathoms, over the ground' (Ming 九 百 度 地行). A fathom (alda) is the span of the arms, about six feet, so the claim is for an extraordinary range.

sentences.t: tatam deližü qarbuγ̇asu tabun žaγ̇ud alda γažar-a qarbuju.

morph.gloss: to pull, draw in (Ming 減了 'reduced'; analysis uncertain) [減了]
to draw (a bow) (Ming 拽; stem uncertain) [拽着]

sentences.l: Reduced having-drawn if-shooting, five hundred fathoms ground-over he-shoots.
sentences.i: Drawn short and shot, it flies five hundred fathoms over the ground.
sentences.n: tatam is glossed 減了, 'reduced', and I read it as 'drawn less, drawn short'; the stem and ending are not clear to me (perhaps tata- 'pull' with an ending -m). tabun žaγud alda γažar-a, 'five hundred fathoms over the ground' (Ming 五 百 度 地行). The pair (nine hundred at full draw, five hundred at a short draw) is a balance, which makes the sense of tatam as 'less' very likely.

sentences.t: Küġün küġün-(n)eče busu gürelkü maṅγus töregsen Žüči-Qasar keġegdejü.

morph.gloss: a kind of python (Ming 蟒名 'name of a python') [蟒名]
Jüchi-Qasar, a man's name (one two-part name) [人名]

sentences.l: Man from-man other, a gürelkü python born, Žüči-Qasar being-called.
sentences.i: A man unlike other men, born a gürelkü python, he is called Jüchi-Qasar.
sentences.n: Küġün küġün-(n)eče busu: 'man, from man other' (Ming 人 人行 別), 'other than from men'. gürelkü maṅγus töregsen: 'a gürelkü python born' (Ming 蟒名 蟒 生了的): gürelkü is glossed 蟒名, 'name of a python', and maṅγus 'python'; töregsen is the past participle of töre- 'be born'. Žüči-Qasar keġegdejü: 'Jüchi-Qasar is called' (Ming 被說有), with the passive -gde-. So Jamuqa says this is Chinggis's brother Qasar. Why he is "born a python" is not given in the words; the Ming says only 蟒.

sentences.t: Tere bijü-že" keġežüġüi.

morph.gloss: to be (present form bijü) [有 也者︀]

sentences.l: That is indeed." he-said.
sentences.i: That is who it is," he said.
sentences.n: tere bijü-že: 'that is, indeed' (Ming 那 有也者); tere 'that, he' and bijü-že, bü- 'be' with the assertion -že. keġežüġüi, 'said'. The closing quotation mark is at bijü-že, the end of Jamuqa's long answer about the man who comes first from behind.

sentences.t: Tende-eče Tajaṅ Qān ügülerün:

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (short form, after a name) [皇帝]

sentences.l: From there Tajaṅ Qān saying:
sentences.i: At that Tayang Qan said:
sentences.n: Tende-eče 'from there' (Ming 自那裏), the ablative -eče on tende; then the usual ügülerün 'saying'.

sentences.t: "Ele tein böġesü aγ̇la-jin ündür temečeje;
sentences.l: "Only so if-it-is, mountain's high let-us-contend;
sentences.i: "If so, let us vie for the heights of the mountain;
sentences.n: ele tein böġesü 'only if that be so' (as in the earlier unit). aγla-jin ündür temečeje: 'mountain's high' (Ming 山的 高) with aγla for aγula (Shiratori's spelling), and temečeje, which the Ming glosses 爭咱, 'let us contend', hortative -je (the shape uncertain). I take 'vie for the high' as 'go up to the highest place', which is the sense of the next unit (deġegši abaridqun, 'go up').

sentences.t: deġegši abaridqun" keġežü aγ̇ula abarin baiba.

morph.gloss: to climb (Ming 登; stem inferred) [登]

sentences.l: upward climb-you" saying, mountain having-climbed stood.
sentences.i: go up higher, all of you," he said, and climbing the mountain he stood there.
sentences.n: deġegši is 'upward' (Ming 往上), deġeg 'upper' with -ši 'toward'. abaridqun is abari- 'climb' with an ending -dqun that I take as an imperative plural (Ming 登您, 'you climb'), like üžedkün above. keġežü, aγula abarin baiba: 'saying, climbing the mountain, stood'. This is the fourth retreat uphill (units 38, 51, 63, 82), with the same words as the last; the fifth, in unit 90, is the last.

sentences.t: Basa Tajaṅ Qān Žamuqa-dāča asaγurun:

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (short form, after a name) [皇帝]
Jamuqa, a man's name [人名 處]

sentences.l: Again Tajaṅ Qān from Žamuqa when-asking:
sentences.i: Again Tayang Qan asked Jamuqa:
sentences.n: Basa 'again' and asaγurun 'when asking', as in the last; the colon is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: "Teġün-ü qoināča aisunqun ken bijü" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: "Of-that from-behind coming who is" he-said.
sentences.i: "Who is it that comes behind them?" he said.
sentences.n: The opening quotation mark is at Teġün-ü, which is Shiratori's this time. teġün-ü qoināča aisunqun ken bijü: 'of that, from behind, coming ones, who are' (Ming 那的 後行 來的 誰 有). keġežüġüi 'he said' closes the question.

sentences.t: Žamuqa ügülerün:
sentences.l: Žamuqa saying:
sentences.i: Jamuqa said:
sentences.n: The same speech-introduction.

sentences.t: "Tere Höġelün eke-jin nilqa köġün Ödčigin heligetü keġegdejü.

morph.gloss: young, small, the youngest (Ming 最少) [最少的]

sentences.l: "That Höġelün mother's youngest son, Ödčigin, liver-having, is-called.
sentences.i: "That is Mother Högelün's youngest son, Ödchigin, who is called the one with a liver.
sentences.n: Tere Höġelün eke-jin nilqa köġün Ödčigin: 'that, Högelün, mother's youngest son, Ödchigin' (Ming 那 母名 母的 最少的 子 人名); nilqa is 'the youngest' (最少的, 'the least'). heligetü keġegdejü: 'liver-having, is called' (Ming 肝有的 被說有), the possessive -tü on helige 'liver'. The Ming 肝 and the possessive suggest a man with a liver, which I take as an idiom for courage (compare the 'heart' in the dog's portrait), but the Ming does not say so.

sentences.t: Erte untaγči oraj-a bosuγči baruγ̇an-ača ber ülü qočoruju;

morph.gloss: multitude, crowd (Ming 多處 'the many') [多處]
to be left behind (Ming 落後) [落後]

sentences.l: Early sleeper, at-evening (late) riser, from-the-multitude even not left-behind;
sentences.i: He is an early sleeper and a late riser, and even so he is not left behind among the many;
sentences.n: erte untaγči, oraj-a bosuγči: 'early, a sleeper; at evening, a riser' (Ming 早行 睡的, 晩行 起的), with the agent ending -γči, 'one who'. This is strange: 'sleeps early, rises in the evening'. I translate it as it stands (a man who sleeps early and rises late) but suspect that the Ming has the sense of 'when he sleeps, whenever he rises', that is, always ready. baruγan-ača ber ülü qočoruju: 'from the many even not left behind' (Ming 多處 也 不 落後), with ber 'even'.

sentences.t: baidal-ača ber ülü qočodajin" keġežüġüi.

morph.gloss: standing place, position (Ming 立處) [立處]
to be left behind (Ming 落後有) [落後有]

sentences.l: from-the-standing-place even not is-left-behind" he-said.
sentences.i: nor does he fall behind from his post," he said.
sentences.n: baidal-ača ber ülü qočodajin: 'from the standing place even not left behind' (Ming 立處 也 不 落後有). baidal is a place or position where one stands. qočodajin (Ming 落後有) is a different form of qočor-/qočoda- 'be left behind' with an ending I cannot place; the -jin is not the genitive. keġežüġüi 'he said' closes. The point seems to be that he does not lag; how it squares with an early sleeper and late riser I cannot say.

sentences.t: Tajaṅ Qān ügülerün:

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (short form, after a name) [皇帝]

sentences.l: Tajaṅ Qān saying:
sentences.i: Tayang Qan said:
sentences.n: The last speech-introduction of the section.

sentences.t: "Tein böġesü aγ̇la-jin horgil deġere γaruja" keġežüġüi.

morph.gloss: to go up, come out (Ming 上) [上咱]

sentences.l: "So if-it-is, mountain's crown on let-us-go-up" having-said.
sentences.i: "If so, let us go up to the very top of the mountain," he said.
sentences.n: tein böġesü, 'so if it be'; aγla-jin horgil deġere γaruja: 'mountain's crown, on, let us go up' (Ming 山的 頂 上 上咱), with horgil 'crown, summit' (Ming 頂), deġere 'on top' (上) and γaruja, from γar- 'go up' (Ming 上) and the hortative -ja. The Ming has 上 twice, and the first (deġere) is 'on, above' and the second the verb. keġežüġüi 'said'. Tayang's last step uphill is the highest, and the section stops there.
